2_metrics_independent.verification: recomputed from scratch off the shared score cache; identical to the governance record -> the 99.5% recall claim is TRUE on the enriched untouched test (all 4,578 fraud present)

3_4_production_prevalence.derivation: FPR is measured on legit rows only and legit is 99.88% of production traffic, so production alert rate = p*recall + (1-p)*FPR ~= FPR mathematically. A 15.9% FPR DOES imply ~16% production alert rate; the enriched-sample 43% precision/25% alert rate does NOT transfer.
3_4_production_prevalence.conclusion: the earlier claim '~16% of real transactions alerted with 99.5% recall' is mathematically supported at production prevalence; precision at production prevalence is ~0.75%, not 43%. The '<=25% alerts' claim holds ONLY on the enriched evaluation, NOT as a production alert-rate claim

5_cascade.design: stage1 = highest val threshold with val recall>=0.995 (0.02687); stage2 = member-consensus bar b over stage-1 alerts, tuned on val to keep val recall>=0.99 while cutting alerts
5_cascade.stage2_outcome: DEGENERATE — members 0.94-0.97 correlated; no b cuts alerts at val recall>=0.99; complete cascade == stage-1 screen
5_cascade.conclusion: a two-stage consensus cascade does NOT reduce alerts at >=99% recall for this ensemble; the ROC/PR curve is binding, not the architecture

6_segmented.design: segments designed a priori on feature semantics (cold-start/online/pattern-risk/mature-normal), err excluded (constant in deployed regime); per-segment thresholds locked on VALIDATION at segment recall>=0.99
6_segmented.conclusion: segmented thresholds reallocate the same alert budget (slightly higher recall, same FPR) — no segmentation discovered that cuts alerts at >=99% recall

7_temporal_drift_quantified.channel_shift_finding: validation-window fraud is ~94% from 2016 and 86% of 2016 fraud is ONLINE; untouched-test fraud (2018-19) is almost entirely chip/swipe IN-PERSON (2017: 255 fraud; 2020 Jan-Feb: 0 fraud). The v2/v3 thresholds were locked on an online-fraud wave that mostly disappears at test time -> drift is partly channel shift, not pure calendar drift. recall@1%FPR falls 0.458 (2018) -> 0.346 (2019) -> genuine degradation, no-drift claim would be FALSE

8_pr_operating_points.note: PR perspective: at real production prevalence even the strict 1%-FPR point has only ~4% precision; extreme class imbalance (0.12%) dominates every operating point; enriched-sample precision cannot be quoted as production precision
